beats.say: India had its own killer dinosaur, with a horn on its head.
Its name is Rajasaurus, the king lizard, and it hunted in what is now Gujarat.
That was about sixty-seven million years ago, when India was an island drifting north.
In the early nineteen-eighties, a government geologist dug its bones out of a hill near the village of Rahioli.
Then the bones waited nearly twenty years.
In two thousand three, scientists pieced the skull together and named a new meat-eater, somewhere between six and eleven metres long.
Its closest known cousin lived far away, on Madagascar. A clue that the two lands were once joined.
So when someone says the great dinosaurs were all American, tell them about the king from the Narmada.
